note: AI summary written on the ground from the simulator figures only (src/sim, Mouad's data). To be validated by the CMO. Never used to decide on an alert.

days.text: Baseline ground assessment (D0): hip bone density at 100% of the preflight value. This is the starting point for all comparisons. The NASA threshold is 95% of preflight [V1 4027].
Estimated density at 99.32% of preflight, a loss of 0.68%. Loss follows the expected microgravity slope (−0.16 point per week). Status: nominal, above the NASA threshold of 95% [V1 4027].

Estimated density at 98.68% of preflight (loss of 1.32%), trend −0.15 point per week. Still above the 95% threshold [V1 4027]. But at current pace, loss would reach 8.7% at return (D860), out of limits.

Estimated density at 98.01% of preflight (loss of 1.99%), status: monitor. The problem is not today but the trajectory: at current pace, 8.7% loss at return (D860), below the NASA threshold of 95% [V1 4027]. Suggested action: heavy-load ARED, calcium and vitamin D, and raise bisphosphonates with the ground flight surgeon.

Projection on arrival at Mars (Sol 0, D210) at current pace: 96.09% of preflight, a loss of 3.91%. Still within the standard but to monitor, and the slope leads to 8.7% loss at return. Model projection, not a measurement.

Projection at Sol 0 (D210) with the plan followed: 97.37% of preflight, a loss of 2.63%, status: nominal. The plan clearly slows the loss compared with the current pace (3.91%). Model projection, not a measurement.

Projection at return (D860) at current pace: 91.30% of preflight, a loss of 8.70%. This is below the NASA threshold of 95% [V1 4027]: status out of limits. This scenario warrants discussing it now with the ground flight surgeon.

Projection at return (D860) with the plan followed: 95.78% of preflight, a loss of 4.22%. This is just above the NASA threshold of 95% [V1 4027]: status: monitor. The plan halves the loss, but the margin stays thin (bisphosphonates: LeBlanc 2013).
